alternatives.argument: Explicit Gaussian split D/2+Z,D/2-Z defines the procedure, preserves parent sum algebraically, and gives conditional covariance -hI/4. No unavailable source premise is used.

Steps 1.1–2.1 compute the joint Gaussian covariance, factor its characteristic function, and distinguish unconditional independent children from conditional negative covariance. Finite induction in steps 3.1–4.1 proves all fixed-depth laws.
Explicit finite stopping-time partition with F_tau-measurable positive steps and deterministic maximum defines the admissible grid; endpoint decisions are expressly excluded.

Deterministic finite dyadic ceiling approximations of tau wedge t give F_t-measurable finite sums. Continuity and completeness then verify each stopped-sigma test. Watkins is contextual, not a substitute for this local proof.

Upward deterministic dyadic rounding gives predictable finite-step coefficients, squared integral error at most 2 delta E|xi|², and telescoping integral sums. Isometry and continuity identify the stopped increment and indistinguishable versions.

Explicit EM recursion uses left stopped information; endpoint rejection stores its parent and bridge children. The Borel acceptance rule makes bounded trial execution measurable. Separate branch labels prevent a convergence assertion for endpoint refinement.
Induction on the deterministic work counter proves C<=B; measurable finite updates and Borel rejection make C a random variable. Thus EC<=B, and completion is reported only on reaching T.

Truncate each left-endpoint coefficient at |Y_n|<=|X0| vee R, stop at the path exit and tau_k, and apply the stopped-integral identity. Doob, growth, dominated convergence and Gronwall give an R,k-independent supremum second moment. Two Fatou passages remove k and R without an expected step-count assumption.

The stopped-step identity and uniform moment bound give global interpolation integrals. On every stopping interval Doob bounds the integrated diffusion increment by 4mh E(||sigma_n||² h_n); summing nonnegative terms yields O(h) integrated within-step error. State Lipschitzness and half-Hölder time regularity then give, by Doob on the error integral, v(t)=E sup_{r<=t}|e_r|² <= C integral_0^t v + C h. Gronwall proves v(T)<=Ch, which implies both the stated one-time bound and the random-grid-endpoint bound. No deterministic-time estimate is substituted at a random time.
The affine Brownian residual W_t-(t/h)W_h explicitly defines the Gaussian bridge, with fixed endpoints.

The residual path and W_h have zero Gaussian cross covariance and are independent by coordinate-generation. Product Gaussian increments give the density ratio before the terminal time; pi-lambda extends cylinders to Borel path events, and the explicit measurable affine map proves full-path disintegration.

The local reflection supplier gives endpoint joint density p_h(2a-r). The explicit bridge disintegration gives the density ratio almost everywhere. Restriction absolute continuity before h excludes an atom of the bridge maximum at a; uniform endpoint perturbation then proves endpoint continuity and extends the identity to every specified endpoint. Boundary endpoints give probability one.

A geometric sum of independent rejection events gives the truncated Gaussian law; symmetry and conditional second-moment comparison give variance strictly below h. The unchanged bridge parent retains exact sum consistency.
Two explicit half-step EM substitutions yield h² y0/4+h D/4+h Z/2. Independence and stated Gaussian variances give variance h³/8 at zero initial value.
Substitute x=y=h=1 and c=0 into the fully local bridge crossing theorem to obtain exp(-2)>0 despite positive endpoints.
